ontology.comment: Note that the Golgi apparatus can be located in various places in the cytoplasm. description.text:
This entry consists of a number of carbohydrate sulphotransferases that transfer sulphate to carbohydrate groups in glycoproteins and glycolipids. These include:

  • Carbohydrate sulphotransferases 8 and 9, which transfer sulphate to position 4 of non-reducing N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) residues in both N-glycans and O-glycans [[cite:PUB00033954]]. They function in the biosynthesis of glycoprotein hormones lutropin and thyrotropin, by mediating sulphation of their carbohydrate structures.
  • Carbohydrate sulphotransferase 10, which transfers sulphate to position 3 of the terminal glucuronic acid in both protein- and lipid-linked oligosaccharides [[cite:PUB00033955]]. It directs the biosynthesis of the HNK-1 carbohydrate structure, a sulphated glucuronyl-lactosaminyl residue carried by many neural recognition molecules, which is involved in cell interactions during ontogenetic development and in synaptic plasticity in the adult.
  • Carbohydrate sulphotransferases 11 - 13, which catalyze the transfer of sulphate to position 4 of the GalNAc residue of chondroitin [[cite:PUB00033956]]. The orthologue inCaenorhabditis elegansis known as carbohydrate sulfotransferase chst-1 [[cite:PUB00085650]]. Chondroitin sulphate constitutes the predominant proteoglycan present in cartilage and is distributed on the surfaces of many cells and extracellular matrices. Some, thought not all, of these enzymes also transfer sulphate to dermatan.
  • Carbohydrate sulphotransferase D4ST1, which transfers sulphate to position 4 of the GalNAc residue of dermatan sulphate [[cite:PUB00033957]].
  • Heparan sulphate 2-O-sulphotransferase (HS2ST). Heparan sulphate (HS) is a co-receptor for a number of growth factors, morphogens, and adhesion proteins. HS biosynthetic modifications may determine the strength and outcome of HS-ligand interactions. Mice that lack HS2ST undergo developmental failure only after midgestation,the most dramatic effect being the complete failure of kidney development [[cite:PUB00010170]].
  • Heparan-sulphate 6-O-sulphotransferase (HS6ST), which catalyses the transfer of sulphate from adenosine 3'-phosphate, 5'-phosphosulphate to the 6th position of the N -sulphoglucosamine residue in heparan sulphate [[cite:PUB00012826]].
  • Chondroitin 6-sulphotransferase catalyses the transfer of sulphate to position 6 of the N-acetylgalactosamine residue of chondroitin [[cite:PUB00053392]].

summation.displayName: Important functional domains in dermatan or dermatan sulfate...
summation.text: Important functional domains in dermatan or dermatan sulfate (DS) are generated by the action of an epimerase (which converts D-glucuronic acid into its epimer L-iduronic acid) together with 4-O-sulfation. These domains are named 4-O-sulfated iduronic acid blocks (Pachebo et al. 2009). Carbohydrate sulfotransferase 14 (CHST14) (Evers et al. 2001) mediates the transfer of sulfate to position 4 of another N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) residue of D2,4(S)2-PG (sulfated on position 2 of IdoA and position 4 of GalNAc) to produce a further sulfated product D2,4,4(S)3-PG (sulfated on another GalNAc in addition to the ones above). Mutations in CHST14 can cause a form of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDSMC1, MIM:601776; Miyake et al., 2010).

goBiologicalProcess.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of dermatan sulfate proteoglycans, which consist of a core protein linked to a dermatan sulfate glycosaminoglycan. The dermatan sulfate chain is composed of the repeating disaccharide unit beta-(1,4)-D-hexuronic acid-beta-(1,3)-N-acetyl-D-galactosamine. Tthe former can be a mixture of sulfated and nonsulfated D-glucuronic and L-iduronic acids, and the latter can be O-sulfated. Dermatan sulfate chains are covalently linked to serine/threonine residues (O-linked) of the core protein via a tetrasaccharide linker sequence (xylose-galactose-galactose-glucuronate).

summation.text: Dermatan sulfate (DS) glycosaminoglycan chains consist of N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) residues alternating in glycosidic linkages with glucuronic acid (GlcA) or iduronic acid (IdoA) residues. They are bound to the tetrasaccharide linker moiety of core proteins. As with CS, GalNAc residues can be sulfated in DS chains but also the uronic acid residues may be substituted with sulfate at the 2- and 4- positions. summation.text: Carbohydrate sulfotransferase 14 (CHST14) (Evers et al. 2001) mediates the transfer of sulfate to position 4 of N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) residue of dermatan or to a further GalNAc residue of dermatan sulfate (D2,4(S)2-PG) in iduronate rich domains. As 4-O sulfation by CHST14 is essential for DS formation, defective CHST14 results in much lower levels of DS and higher levels of chondroitin sulfate (CS) being produced. DS plays an important role in human development and extracellular matrix maintenance and defective CHST14 results in Ehlers-Danlos syndrome,  musculocontractural type (MIM:601776). Mutations causing this disease include V49*, R213P, R135G/L137Q, Y293, P281L and the compound heterozygotes P281L/K69* and P281L/C285S (Dundar et al. 2009, Miyake et al. 2010).

Plays a pivotal role in the formation of 4-0-sulfated IdoA blocks in dermatan sulfate. annotation_interpretations.reason: The subcellular-location mapping is corroborated by endogenous human MCF10a Golgi colocalization and human D4ST1 fluorescent-fusion overlap with GM130 in COS-7 cells (PMID:29976758). Membrane topology remains sequence-based rather than established by protease protection.

Reactome reaction 2022063 places Q8NCH0 entity 1971536 in the Golgi membrane. Independent human-cell and human-construct microscopy corroborates the compartment (PMID:29976758); type-II topology remains sequence-based.

Reactome disease event 3636919 places a CHST14 mutant set in the Golgi membrane and links to normal reaction 2022063. Retain the modeled compartment with independent WT localization support (PMID:29976758), without claiming correct delivery or activity for every mutant.

PMID:11470797 expresses the sequence-verified human AF401222 376-residue ORF in CHO/Tag cells. Radiolabeled PAPS transfer in extracts and conditioned medium, with mock and C4ST controls and product digestion/chromatography, establishes C4 sulfation of GalNAc adjacent to iduronic acid. These are not homogeneous purified-enzyme assays. PMID:29976758 independently reconstitutes the reaction with affinity-purified human residues 61–376 and DS-epi1.

EC:2.8.2.35 and RHEA:48052 match the authenticated reaction and GO:0001537. Human recombinant sulfate-transfer assays establish GalNAc C4 modification adjacent to iduronic acid (PMID:11470797), independently corroborated by purified human residues 61–376 with DS-epi1 (PMID:29976758). The original CHO/Tag extracts and medium were not homogeneous enzyme preparations.

Reactome 2022063 identifies catalyst 2022068/Q8NCH0 entity 1971536 and the PAPS-to-PAP/dermatan-sulfation reaction. Direct human recombinant biochemistry independently supports this normal catalytic step (PMID:11470797); the original experiment used extracts and medium, not homogeneous purified enzyme.

Reactome 3636919 is a failed CHST14-mutant reaction with no productive output, linked to normalReaction 2022063. The unqualified gene-level capability is retained from WT primary biochemistry (PMID:11470797); this does not assign activity to the defective variants. Patient-cell evidence supplies disease context (PMID:20004762).

Three exact MINT records connect human CHST14/Q8NCH0 to CFTR/P13569: a traditional MaMTH record attributed to Figure EV5 and WT/F508del MaMTH-HTS records attributed to Dataset EV2 (PMID:35156780). HEK293 host, fusion tags and the CFTR position-508 deletion remain explicit. GO:0044325 requires binding to a transmembrane transporter, an established CFTR class; it does not require CHST14 to regulate transport. Retain this useful assay-level refinement at non-core prominence. A proposed native Golgi/channel mechanism is neither required by the term nor demonstrated, and CHST14-specific co-IP or purified binary binding is not claimed. Supported generic NC decisions elsewhere do not prohibit a definition-compatible class refinement here.

ARBA00028708 includes IPR005331 plus Primates, matching the human protein. Endogenous human-cell and human-construct microscopy independently supports Golgi localization (PMID:29976758); this corroborates the location without upgrading sequence-based topology to a direct protection assay.

The original GO:0008146 assertion is correct: CHST14 transfers sulfate from PAPS to a carbohydrate hydroxyl. The proposed GO:0001537 specifies the target reaction directly demonstrated by human recombinant assays (PMID:11470797; PMID:29976758). This is target-level curation under the guideline to refine overly broad terms, not a claim that dermatan specificity arose at PTN000951429 or that its historical IBD placement is wrong. Family membership and WITH/FROM composition do not reconstruct that node. Existing specific annotations corroborate the reaction; this replacement adds no NEW annotation and changes no source evidence or qualifier.

The authentic ARBA00028338 condition set uses IPR005331/IPR018011 with Eukaryota, and those InterPro entries map the broad, correct sulfotransferase capability. Human CHST14 assays establish the dermatan-specific reaction (PMID:11470797; PMID:29976758), supporting target-level refinement to GO:0001537. The recommendation does not rewrite the rule output or claim every family member shares dermatan specificity. It refines an existing target annotation; the already accepted specific rows are corroborating coverage, not a new assertion.

IPR005331/IPR018011 support the broad membrane assignment. The predicted type-II precursor and independent Golgi microscopy are compatible with that location (PMID:11470797; PMID:29976758). Retaining a correct compartment here does not prohibit an informative target-specific catalytic refinement in a separate MF review.

The original paper predicts an N-terminal membrane segment and type-II topology. Most recombinant activity is in medium; suggested proteolytic shedding remains untested and does not negate the full-length membrane precursor (PMID:11470797). Independent Golgi microscopy supports membrane localization (PMID:29976758), without establishing native topology by protease protection.

The IPR018011 mapping correctly captures carbohydrate biosynthesis. Human CHST14 itself performs the PAPS-dependent sulfation of the dermatan chain, so GO:0050651 is a more informative process than generic carbohydrate synthesis. It does not assign backbone polymerization or epimerase catalysis to CHST14. This refines an existing source assertion and duplicates no new process proposal.

PMID:11470797 identifies putative PAPS 5-prime-phosphosulfate and 3-prime-phosphate contact regions by sequence comparison; its Discussion calls those assignments hypotheses. GO:0042301 names phosphate-ion binding. Contacts with phosphate groups covalently contained in PAPS do not establish that separate ligand activity. Retain MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED for this extrapolation: the source neither assays free phosphate-ion binding nor provides a negative result that would establish its biochemical impossibility. The demonstrated sulfate-transfer reaction is unaffected.

Human recombinant CHST14 transfers sulfate onto the dermatan chain, directly performing a biosynthetic chemical step (PMID:11470797); later purified-component work corroborates that role (PMID:29976758). The original acts_upstream_of_or_within qualifier is broad enough to include participation within the process, so it is not contradicted by this evidence. It understates the more precise involved_in interpretation used in the core and sibling source, but remains preserved as the historical qualifier. Patient fibroblast changes corroborate dermatan-sulfate deficiency (PMID:20004762), without assigning every developmental consequence to the enzyme.

Reactome 2022923 contains the target reaction 2022063 alongside epimerization, other sulfation and secretion events. CHST14 directly catalyzes its own sulfate-transfer step; this is more specific than mere membership in the pathway and does not transfer other enzymes or transporters activities to CHST14.

The current PTN002637560 assertion correctly records dermatan metabolism. Human biochemical evidence supports the more informative biosynthetic direction, GO:0050651 (PMID:11470797; PMID:29976758). Q8NCH0 self-inclusion is legitimate experimental grounding, not circularity. Its being the sole listed extant source does not establish the breadth or placement of the historical ancestral node; neither the tree nor MSA was reconstructed. The replacement is a target-level refinement, not a revised historical IBD assertion.

The original IDA source directly assays sulfate transfer in the biosynthetic direction, not dermatan degradation. The narrower GO:0050651 is supported by the performed chemical step and human reconstitution/cellular evidence. The existing metabolic assertion is sound but less informative; its source fields remain unchanged.

The authentic publisher Table S2 row 389 identifies CHST14/IPI00044326.3 with two sequences, two spectra and 9.3% sequence coverage. Table S1 rows 3817–3818 supply the two peptide sequences, both matching the current Q8NCH0 sequence. Actual Methods describe a single human donor, a 200,000g exosome-rich pellet and MudPIT protein-group analysis; this is not CHST14-specific vesicle imaging or an enzyme-activity assay. Retain the original HDA location without inferring exosome biogenesis or a defining extracellular catalytic role. The full normal-fetch variant and original tables were inspected separately from the unchanged, less complete main cache.
